works.why: Smudged charcoal and ghostly erasures on screen: hand-drawn animation shown as projected video art.

works.title: History of the Main Complaint
works.hook: Stars Soho Eckstein, the greedy businessman who returns again and again in his films.
works.why: Black and white charcoal animation projected in the gallery: drawing turned into moving-image art.

works.title: I am not me, the horse is not mine
works.hook: Eight films play at once across the walls, drawing on 1920s and 1930s Russian avant-garde.
works.why: Several projections surround the viewer at once: video art grown into an immersive multi-screen space.

works.title: Bear
works.hook: A silent black and white film of two naked men, one of them McQueen, circling each other.
works.why: Silent black and white film projected in the gallery: video art that asks you to watch closely.

works.title: Caribs' Leap/Western Deep
works.hook: Two films made for documenta 11 in 2002: Caribbean islanders who leapt to their deaths, and miners deep under South Africa.
works.why: Big projections on several screens in a dark room: film made for the gallery, not the cinema.

works.title: End Credits
works.hook: A homage to the singer and activist Paul Robeson, built from scanned files.
works.why: Documents scroll on a projected screen: video art that turns an archive into a slow moving image.

works.title: Portrait as an Escapologist
works.hook: A still photograph, from an artist better known for moving images.
works.why: One frozen frame, lit and framed like a film shot: the cinematic eye behind his gallery films.

works.title: Queen and Country
works.hook: Families chose the portraits for stamp sheets honouring UK service personnel killed in Iraq.
works.why: An oak cabinet of stamp sheets you pull out one by one: a memorial you handle, made by an artist of moving images.

works.title: DOB in the Strange Forest (Blue DOB)
works.hook: The ring of colourful mushrooms refers to the atomic bomb.
works.why: A cute cartoon character with bold outlines and flat colour, turned into 3D: Superflat's anime look.

works.title: Flower Matango (b)
works.hook: About four metres tall, made of fibreglass, resin and lacquer between 2001 and 2006.
works.why: Smiling cartoon flowers with glossy, flat colour: Superflat cuteness blown up to monument size.

works.title: Warp
works.hook: Platinum and gold leaf shine across a canvas almost three metres tall.
works.why: Gold leaf and flat graphic shapes: old Japanese screen painting meets anime, the Superflat mix.

works.title: In the Land of the Dead, Stepping on the Tail of a Rainbow
works.hook: About 25 metres long, it borrows Taoist hermits from an 18th-century Japanese painter.
works.why: Edo-period figures redrawn with comic-book energy and flat colour: Superflat links old and new Japan.

works.title: Brigid Polk (305)
works.hook: Soft edges everywhere, so the portrait looks like a photo slightly out of focus.
works.why: A soft blur over a photo-like portrait: Richter's photo paintings, copying everyday images.

works.title: Elizabeth I
works.hook: A grey, blurred image of a smiling face that looks like a newspaper photo.
works.why: A grey, photo-like, blurred image: the borrowed pictures of Capitalist Realism.

works.title: St John
works.hook: Oil on canvas, with layers of colour scraped across each other so earlier ones show through.
works.why: Colour scraped in wide bands: the squeegee abstracts Richter turned to in the 1980s.

works.title: Abstract Painting (726)
works.hook: Streaks of colour dragged across the canvas, leaving gaps and ridges.
works.why: Streaks and ridges of dragged paint: Richter's squeegee abstracts.

works.title: Abstract Painting (Grey) (880-3)
works.hook: Oil on aluminium: grey paint dragged across the surface in thin vertical streaks.
works.why: Scraped, layered grey: Richter's abstract paintings, far from his early photo works.

works.title: Untitled (London Bridge)
works.hook: A crowded, sunny scene around a bridge, every figure painted in Marshall's deep black.
works.why: Figures painted a deep, pure black in a bright, busy scene: Marshall's signature.

works.title: Primordial Chaos, No. 16
works.hook: From her very first abstract series, begun in 1906.
works.note: Part of the Paintings for the Temple, which she made between 1906 and 1915.
works.why: Loops and spirals float on deep blue with nothing recognisable: an early step into pure abstraction.

works.title: The Swan, No. 17
works.hook: Never shown in her lifetime.
works.note: In the Swan series, birds slowly turn into pure geometric shapes.
works.why: A circle split into black, white, yellow and blue on flat red: shape and colour alone carry the meaning.

works.title: Group X, No. 2, Altarpiece
works.hook: One of the Altarpieces in her Paintings for the Temple.
works.note: A gold disc sits above a dark triangle, painted for a temple she never saw built.
works.why: A gold disc above a striped triangle, with no figures at all: geometry used as a spiritual symbol.

works.title: The Dove, No. 1
works.hook: The dove stood for love in her private symbolism.
works.note: Part of the Paintings for the Temple.
works.why: A pale circle with a heart shape and a band of rainbow colours: symbols, not things you could see.

works.title: The Swan, No. 9
works.hook: Pairs of opposites, light and dark, meet in the middle.
works.note: The swan stood for transcendence in her private symbolism.
works.why: Two curving forms, one dark and one light, meet on flat red: abstract shapes standing for opposites.

works.title: Late Summer (Eftersommar)
works.hook: The kind of landscape she showed in public while keeping her abstract work private.
works.note: Painted three years before her first abstract series.

works.title: Self-Portrait at the Age of 63
works.hook: Painted in the last year of his life, with no flattery at all.

works.title: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr Nicolaes Tulp
works.hook: The anatomist Dr Tulp shows the muscles of an arm to a group of onlookers.

works.title: The Jewish Bride
works.hook: A tender couple in thick, glowing paint. Van Gogh is said to have adored it.

works.title: The Return of the Prodigal Son
works.hook: A late work: a father welcomes home his ragged son.

works.title: A Woman Bathing in a Stream
works.hook: Quick, loose brushwork, almost like a sketch.

works.title: Syndics of the Drapers' Guild
works.hook: Cloth inspectors look up as if we have just walked in.

works.title: Little Girl in a Blue Armchair
works.hook: A bored child sprawls in a big armchair. Degas worked on the background.

works.title: Woman with a Pearl Necklace in a Loge
works.hook: A young woman at the theatre, lit up and reflected in the mirror behind her.

works.title: In the Loge
works.hook: She looks through her opera glasses while a man in the background looks at her.

works.title: The Letter
works.hook: A colour print from her set of ten inspired by Japanese prints.

works.title: The Boating Party
works.hook: Bold flat shapes and a high horizon, learned from Japanese prints.

works.title: Lady at the Tea Table
works.place: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
works.hook: An older relative presides over a blue and gold tea set.

works.title: A Corner of the Artist's Room in Paris
works.hook: No one is there: just a chair, a table and soft light from the window.

works.title: Young Woman Holding a Black Cat
works.hook: A still, seated woman in soft greys and blues, painted with a dry, chalky touch.

works.title: Dorelia in a Black Dress
works.hook: Her friend Dorelia McNeill stands quietly in a dark room, hands folded.

works.title: Composition VIII
works.hook: Painted at the Bauhaus: crisp circles, lines and triangles.

works.title: Several Circles
works.hook: Glowing, overlapping circles float on a dark ground.

works.title: Accent in Pink
works.hook: Circles of colour scattered over a tilted yellow shape.

works.title: The Blue Rider
works.hook: An early work: a rider in a blue cloak gallops across a meadow.

works.title: Blue Mountain
works.hook: Riders and a mountain are still there, but colour is taking over.
